## Module Overview

### Module summary

Download bird models for BCR units intersecting the study area, optionally selecting
species, and publish an index of the downloaded files. Model files must follow
`SPECIES_canBCR.Rdata`, for example `GCKI_can12.Rdata`. Species codes are
case-insensitive letters/digits starting with a letter; BCR codes are digits.
Google Drive access uses the caller's existing googledrive authentication.
The loader explicitly visits the root folder and each nested species folder,
tracking folder IDs to avoid repeat visits. It does not rely on a single combined
recursive listing. Folder-listing errors stop acquisition before downloading;
Drive shortcuts are not followed.

### Module inputs and parameters

Supply a polygon `studyArea` and optionally `BCRdata` (a polygon SpatVector with
valid `subUnit` identifiers). Otherwise BCR boundaries are downloaded by
`.inputObjects`. Supply `modelfolderURL` as a shared input to override the default
Google Drive folder; the legacy parameter of the same name is not used for acquisition.

Set the module's `species` parameter to select one or several species:

```{r select-species}
parameters <- list(bird_modelLoad = list(species = c("GCKI", "RCKI")))
# Use species = "GCKI" for one species, or character(0) (default) for all species.
```

Species codes are trimmed, uppercased, and deduplicated. Every requested species
must have a Canadian model for every intersecting BCR. Only filenames containing
`_can` and ending in `.Rdata` are candidates for validation. US models
(`SPECIES_usaBCR.Rdata`) and other unrelated files are ignored, as in the original
Canadian-only loader. Missing pairs, unparseable Canadian model
names, duplicate selected species/BCR keys, or BCRs without models stop acquisition
before any model downloads.

`testModelLimit = NA` downloads all matches. A positive whole number limits models
per BCR in filename order **after** species selection; it must be at least the
number of explicitly selected species. Download destinations use `inputPath(sim)`;
the existing `overwrite = TRUE` policy is retained.

Geometry validation runs before model acquisition, with BCR validity checked
after any reprojection. Invalid inputs report feature numbers and reasons.
Invalid BCR geometry is repaired automatically; no repair parameter is needed.

Repair emits a warning because polygon boundaries may change. It applies
`terra::makeValid()` to invalid BCR features on a local copy, checks validity,
nonempty polygon area, feature count and attributes, and uses the repaired
geometry for intersections and `BCR_parts`. The original shared `BCRdata` is
not modified. Invalid `studyArea` geometry is never repaired automatically.
If repair cannot preserve valid nonempty polygons, feature count, and attributes,
the loader stops before downloading models.

### Module outputs

`sim$modelIndex` is a data.table keyed by `species` and `BCR`, with one row per
successfully downloaded file. Its five columns are character vectors:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `species` | Uppercase species code, e.g. `GCKI` |
| `BCR` | BCR subUnit identifier, without leading zeros, e.g. `"12"` |
| `fileName` | Remote model filename |
| `localPath` | Absolute path to the downloaded file; existence is checked |
| `remoteId` | Google Drive file ID |

```{r inspect-model-index}
sim$modelIndex[species == "GCKI" & BCR == "12"]
sim$modelIndex[species %in% c("GCKI", "RCKI")]
```

The existing outputs remain available: `modelFiles` is the character vector of
local paths in index order; `BCR_codes` is a character vector of intersecting BCR
identifiers; `BCR_parts` is a SpatVector of clipped BCR polygons, retaining original
attributes. Failed downloads do not publish a completed index.

```{r moduleOutputs-bird-modelLoad, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}

```

### Links to other modules

Study-area polygons may be supplied by bird_dataPrep. This change publishes the
loader index only: bird_modelPredict still scans its configured model folder
and does not yet consume `modelIndex` (workplan ML-H3). Species filtering here
does not remove previously downloaded models from a shared folder.
